1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```

2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset. 

```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+geom_bar()+theme_classic()
```

3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+geom_bar(fill="#223030")+theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill="#E8D9CD"), plot.background=element_rect(fill="#E8D9CD"),element_text(size=.1), plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5))+ylab("Frequency")+xlab("Eye Color")+ggtitle("Frequency of Eye Colors")
```

4. Create a graph displaying information about character's height in each homeworld. 

```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, homeworld))+geom_point()
```

5. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, homeworld))+geom_point(fill="#DD8E58")+theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill="#e5d1b8"), plot.background=element_rect(fill="#e5d1b8"), plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5))+xlab("Character height")+ylab("Character homeworld")+ggtitle("Character and their homeworld")
```

6. Create a graph of character's height by mass. 

```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, color=mass))+geom_bar()+theme_classic()
```


7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, color=mass))+geom_bar(position=position_dodge(), fill="#680c0a")+theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill="#cdb9b1"), plot.background = element_rect(fill="#ab8b6d"), plot.title=element_text(hjust=0.5))+labs(x="Height of character", y="Mass of character", title="Mass and height of character")
```


8. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, color=mass, fill=gender))+geom_bar(position=position_dodge())
```


9. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, color=mass, fill=gender))+geom_bar(position=position_dodge())+theme(plot.title=element_text(hjust=0.5))+labs(x="Height of character", y="Mass of character", title="Mass and height of character", fill="Gender of character")
```
